Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:10:1.hebrew: מיעט סם - שלא יתן סם על אזנו וינקבנה, דהא לא דמי למרצע, שאינו נוקב מכח אדם אלא מאליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:10:1.english: It restricted a corrosive substance - That one may not place a corrosive substance on his ear and have it pierce it, for this is not similar to an awl, since [the substance] does not pierce by a person's force, but on its own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:11:1.hebrew: הירך מיומן שבירך - בפרק גיד הנשה (חולין צ:) ר' יהודה אומר: אין נוהג אלא באחת, והדעת מכרעת שהיא של ימין. ויליף לה מה"א דהירך, ודרש: הירך — חשובה שבירכות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:11:1.english: “The thigh” — the right-hand one (meyumman) of the thighs - In the chapter of Gid HaNasheh (Chullin 90b), Rabbi Yehuda says that [the prohibition of the sciatic nerve] applies only to one [thigh], and reason decides that it is the right one. He derives this from the letter heh of “the thigh” (hayarech), and expounds: “The thigh” — the most prominent of the thighs.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:12:1.hebrew: ויעשה בעל מום - ומה בכך? והלא רציעה מצוה היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:12:1.english: And let him be rendered blemished - And what of it? Surely piercing is a commandment!

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:13:1.hebrew: חידוש הוא - שהתיר שפחה כנענית לישראל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:13:1.english: It is a novelty - That [the Torah] permitted a Canaanite maidservant to an Israelite.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:15:1.hebrew: באיסקונדרי איטלליתו - לא הטיתם לב לדקדק בשמועתכם, אלא כמשחקין בפספסין, שנקראים מרייל"ש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:15:1.english: With tokens [iskundri] you played - You did not set your heart to be precise in your learning, but [acted] like those who play with tokens, [called in Old French] mareil.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:16:1.hebrew: וא"ת אין רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית - למה לי טעמא דרבנן מפני שנעשה בעל מום? בלאו הכי נמי לא שייך רציעה, דבעינן שיאמר ״אהבתי את אדוני את אשתי״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:16:1.english: And if you say that his master does not give him a Canaanite maidservant - Why do I need the reason [of the Rabbis], that he became blemished? Even without it, piercing is not applicable, since we require [that he say], "I love my master, my wife":

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:16:2.hebrew: תו לא מידי - אין להשיב על זאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:16:2.english: Nothing more - There is nothing [further] to answer to this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:17:1.hebrew: כהן - מהו ביפת תואר, לפי שהכהן אסור בגיורת שהיתה זונה קודם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:17:1.english: A priest - [The question is whether he may take a beautiful captive woman, since] a priest is forbidden to a convert woman who had previously been a zonah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:17:2.english: What [is the law] regarding a beautiful woman - in war.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:17:3.english: Permitted - As [the Gemara] explains as it proceeds.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:18:1.hebrew: דברה תורה - לא התירתה אלא בשביל יצר הרע, שאם לא יתירה, יעבור על האזהרה, כדיליף לקמיה מדכתיב ״יפת תואר״, שיצר הרע מתגרה בו. הילכך, בכהן נמי איכא למיחש ליצר הרע, ושריא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:18:1.english: The Torah spoke - It permitted it only on account of the evil inclination, for if it would not permit it, he would transgress the prohibition, as [the Gemara] derives below from the fact that it is written "a beautiful woman," [which shows] that the evil inclination provokes him. Therefore, with a priest too, there is reason to be concerned about the evil inclination, and it is permitted.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:19:1.english: With regard to the second act of intercourse - For his spirit has already cooled.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:1:1.hebrew: ההוא - "בכל ארץ אחוזתכם גאולה תתנו" (ויקרא כה, כד), תלה ביה קרא לקובעו חובה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:1:1.english: That - [The verse] "In all [the land of your possession you shall grant] redemption" (Leviticus 25:24) — the verse linked it to this [case], in order to establish it as an obligation:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:1:2.hebrew: ואפי' לרבי יהושע - אפילו דאמר גבי שדה אחוזה רשות, הכא מודה דחובה, דלא יטמע בעובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:1:2.english: And even according to Rabbi Yehoshua - who said with regard to an inherited field that [redeeming it] is optional, here he agrees that it is an obligation, so that [the Hebrew slave] will not be assimilated among the gentiles.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:20:1.hebrew: והבאתה אל תוך ביתך - פירוש לקיימה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:20:1.english: “Then you shall bring her home to your house” - [This means] to keep her [as a wife].

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:20:2.hebrew: קרינא ביה וראית בשביה - הותרה לו במה שנתן עיניו בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:20:2.english: We read with regard to it: “And you see among the captives” - She became permitted to him by virtue of his having set his eyes upon her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:21:1.hebrew: בשעת שביה - אם נתן מתחילה עיניו בה, ולא שלקחה למוכרה או לשפחה, ואח"כ נתן עיניו בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:21:1.english: At the time of her captivity - If he set his eyes on her from the outset, and not that he took her to sell her or as a maidservant and afterward set his eyes on her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:21:2.hebrew: יפת תואר - משמע: מתוך שמתגרה בה יצרו מחמת יופיה, התירה לו, ובקושי. אלא דמוטב שיאכלו ישראל בשר תמותות שחוטה, בשר מסוכנת שחוטה, ואע"פ שהיא מאוסה, כדכתיב ביחזקאל: ״ולא בא בפי בשר פגול״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:21:2.english: A beautiful woman - This implies: since his evil inclination is provoked toward her by reason of her beauty, [the Torah] permitted her to him, and [only] with difficulty. Rather, [the reason is] that it is preferable that Israel eat the meat of animals that died [of natural causes] but were slaughtered — the meat of a dangerously ill animal that was slaughtered — even though it is repulsive, as it is written in Ezekiel: "And no piggul meat has come into my mouth."

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:21:3.hebrew: ולא יאכלו בשר תמותות - לאחר שימותו ויהו נבלות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:21:3.english: And [Jews should] not eat the flesh of animals that died on their own - After they die and become carcasses.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:5:1.hebrew: סול - פירושו ברוק"א (שפוד, קנה עץ מחודד) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:5:1.english: Sol - [It is] a broca (a spit, a sharpened wooden reed) in the vernacular (Old French).

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:5:3.english: Auger - Tariada (in Old French) (tarière: an auger).

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:5:4.hebrew: מכתב - גרייפ"א (גרפי"א: מַכְתֵּב, חרט), שחוקקין בפנקסיהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:5:4.english: A stylus - Graipa (grafia: stylus, engraving tool), with which they engrave in their writing tablets.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:6:1.hebrew: מרצע הגדול - לקמיה מפרש מאי גמרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:6:1.english: The large awl - Below [the Gemara] explains what the teaching is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:1.hebrew: יודן בריבי - יודן שמו, וגדול בדורו היה, וכל היכא דקרי ליה "בריבי", לשון חכמה וחריפות הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:1.english: Yudan the Distinguished - Yudan was his name, and he was a great man in his generation; and wherever he is called "Ribbi," it is an expression of wisdom and sharpness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:2.hebrew: אלא במילתא - אליה של אזן בבשר ולא בתנוך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:2.english: Only in the miltah - The soft part of the ear, in the flesh, and not in the earlobe.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:3.hebrew: וחכ"א כו' - חולקין עליו, וזו ראיה שלהם: קים לן דאין עבד עברי כהן נרצע, מפני שנעשה בעל מום ולא יכול עוד לשוב לחיזוק הראשון. ולקמיה ילפינן "ושב אל משפחתו" — למוחזק שבמשפחתו. והיאך הוא נעשה בעל מום? והתנן (בכורות דף לז.) גבי מומין: נפגמה אזנו מן הסחוס, אבל לא מן העור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:3.english: And the Sages say, etc. - They disagree with him, and this is their proof: We hold that a Hebrew slave who is a priest is not pierced, because he becomes blemished and can no longer return to his original strength. And below we derive [from the verse] "and he shall return to his family" — [that it refers] to the established status within his family. But how does he become blemished? Surely we learned in a Mishnah (Bekhorot 37a) regarding blemishes: If his ear is notched in the cartilage, [it is a blemish], but not [if notched] in the skin:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:4.hebrew: הא אין רוצעים כו' - הרי יש לך ללמוד מכאן שאין רוצעין אלא בגובה של אזן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:4.english: But they do not pierce, etc. - Behold, you can learn from here that they pierce only in the upper part of the ear.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:5.hebrew: במאי קא מיפלגי - גבי סול וסירא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:7:5.english: With regard to what do they disagree? - Concerning the sol and the sira [the awl and the thorn].

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:8:1.hebrew: דריש כללי ופרטי - בכל התורה, מקום שכולל ופורט, דורש שהפרט פירוש של כלל, ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט. וכי חזר וכלל, לא הוסיף לך בכלל האחרון אלא הדומה לפרט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:8:1.english: He expounds generalizations and details - Throughout the Torah, where [a verse] states a generalization and then specifies a detail, he expounds that the detail is an explanation of the generalization, and the generalization includes only what is in the detail. And when [the verse] again states a generalization, the final generalization adds for you only what is similar to the detail.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:9:1.hebrew: ריבויי ומיעוטי - אין הפרט פירושו של כלל, שתאמר אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, אלא למעוטי הוא בא. לפי שבכלל היה מרבה את הכל, ובא המיעוט אחריו לומר: בזה וכיוצא בו כללתי לך. הילכך, אפילו לא חזר וכלל, הייתי מביא כעין הפרט. וכי חזר וריבה, ריבה הכל, ולא מיעט לך אלא דבר אחד, ומסרו הכתוב לחכמים איזה דבר הראוי למעט מן הכלל. פי' מיעט — ממעט קצת ממשמעו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21b:9:1.english: Amplifications and restrictions - The particular is not an explanation of the general, such that you would say that the general includes only what is in the particular. Rather, it comes to restrict. For the general would have amplified to include everything, and the restriction comes after it to say: I included for you this and its like. Therefore, even if [the verse] had not returned and stated a general term, I would derive [only] something similar to the particular. But when it returned and amplified, it amplified to include everything, and it excluded for you only one thing, and Scripture handed over to the Sages [the determination of] which thing is fitting to exclude from the general. Meaning: "it restricted" — it restricts somewhat from its [full] implication:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:1:1.hebrew: לקובעו חובה ואפילו לר' יהושע - פירש בקונטרס: ואפי' לרבי יהושע דאמר לגבי שדה אחוזה רשות, הכא מודה דהוי חובה, כי היכי דלא יטמע בין העובדי כוכבים. והכא לא שייך לאקשויי "מאי בכל", דהא לא נכתב בההיא עניינא. אך הקשה ה"ר שמואל מקוצי: כיון דמוקי לה כרבי יהושע, ע"כ לא חזי לקובעו חובה אלא בע"ע בלבד, וא"כ אין הריבוי דבכל ארץ אחוזתכם שוה, שהרי לענין בתי ערי חומה אין מרבה קביעות חובה, ולענין ע"ע הוא מרבה חובה; וא"כ הוה ליה למימר בתי החצרים וע"ע הנמכר לעובד כוכבים ולקובעו חובה בשתיהן, וכר"א, ואז הוי ריבוי שוה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:1:1.english: "To establish it as an obligation, even according to Rabbi Yehoshua" - Rashi explained: Even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who said with regard to a field of one's holding that [redemption] is optional, here he concedes that it is an obligation, so that [the Jew] not be assimilated among the gentiles. And here it is not applicable to ask, "What is [the purpose of the word] 'in all'?", since it was not written in that context. But Rabbi Shmuel of Coucy objected: Since [the Gemara] establishes it according to Rabbi Yehoshua, necessarily [the verse] could serve to establish an obligation only in the case of a Hebrew slave alone, and if so, the extension of "in all the land of your holding" is not uniform, for with regard to houses in walled cities it does not extend to establishing an obligation, whereas with regard to a Hebrew slave it does extend an obligation; and if so, [the verse] should have said [that the extension applies to] houses in unwalled villages and to a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, and to establish an obligation in both of them, in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, and then the extension would be uniform:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:20:1.hebrew: בביאה שניה כ"ע לא פליגי דאסור - ואף ע"ג דגבי שפחה לא מפליג בין ביאה ראשונה לשניה, דאף ביאה שניה שריא, דהא איתותב שמואל לעיל — התם היינו טעמא דהוי חידוש: שהותר איסור "לא יהיה קדש" גבי ישראל, הותר נמי גבי כהן. אבל הכא, דכי שריא גבי ישראל אין כאן חידוש, ולגבי כהן אסורה מטעם זונה. ואע"פ שמתגיירת בעל כרחה, עשאה הכתוב כגיורת גמורה, ואכתי איכא איסורא לגבי כהן, ולא מצינו שהתיר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:20:1.english: "With regard to the second act of intercourse, everyone agrees that it is prohibited" - And even though with regard to a maidservant [the Gemara] does not distinguish between the first and second act of intercourse, since even the second act is permitted, for Shmuel was refuted above — there the reason is that it is a novelty: that the prohibition of "there shall not be a [male] prostitute" was permitted in the case of an Israelite, it was permitted also in the case of a priest. But here, when she is permitted to an Israelite there is no novelty, and with regard to a priest she is forbidden on account of [the prohibition of] a zonah. And although she converts against her will, the verse made her like a full convert, and there is still a prohibition with regard to a priest, and we have not found that [the Torah] permitted it.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:21:1.hebrew: אשת אפילו אשת איש - ואע"פ דאין אישות בכותית, כדאיתא פ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נב:), מ"מ איכא עשה, דכתיב (בראשית ב׳:כ״ד): ודבק באשתו, ולא באשת חבירו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:21:1.english: “A woman” — even a married woman - And even though there is no marriage with a gentile woman, as stated in the chapter “Arba Mitot” (Sanhedrin 52b), nevertheless there is a positive commandment, as it is written (Genesis 2:24): “And he shall cleave to his wife” — and not to the wife of his fellow:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:2:1.hebrew: ההוא לקרוב קרוב קודם - ושלשה "יגאלנו" אתי: חד לגופיה, וחד בבתי החצרים ובשדה אחוזה דכתב בחד קרא, וחד למדרש "יגאלנו" לזה ולא לאחר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 21b:2:1.english: That [verse is to teach that] the closer relative comes first - And there are three [instances of] "yigaleinu" that come: one for its own matter, one for houses in open areas and an ancestral field, which are written in one verse, and one to expound "yigaleinu" as [meaning] this one [redeems] and not another:
